items.headline: FDA Approves First Plasmid…
summaries: U.S. Food and Drug Administration reports: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) for treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), a rare disease caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) that leads to the formation of small, wart-like growths in the patient’s airways.

U.S. Food and Drug Administration reports: This approval, the first for a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the U.S., offers patients a new therapeutic option that targets the root cause of RRP and has been shown to reduce the burden of surgical intervention, representing an important step forward for a patient population with limited treatment options.

U.S. Food and Drug Administration reports: The agency based this accelerated approval on clinical trial data showing Voceryq helps reduce the frequency of surgical procedures required to remove growths in adult patients with RRP — an intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

items.headline: PCE price increases reported
summaries: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reports: Personal income increased $54.5 billion (0.2 percent at a monthly rate) in September, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).

U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reports: Disposable personal income (DPI)—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $52.7 billion (0.2 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $113.1 billion (0.5 percent).
U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reports: From the preceding month, the PCE price index for September increased 0.5 percent.

items.headline: FTC, Washington Take Action…
summaries: Federal Trade Commission reports: Small businesses also will be able to rescind processing agreements without a termination penalty under the proposed order settling the FTC and Washington’s allegations.

Federal Trade Commission reports: The FTC and Washington allege that Riverside’s sales pitches included a quote sheet that compared the costs prospective clients paid their existing payment processor with the amount they would save if they used Riverside’s services instead.

Federal Trade Commission reports: The FTC alleges that Riverside’s practices violated the FTC Act and the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act by obtaining consumers’ financial information by using false or fraudulent statements.
